newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures contract on TIFFE ended Thursday's day session lower on profit-taking, traders said.
The June contract closed down 0.04 at 99.18, after moving between 99.18 and 99.22.
"The June opened at the day's high in line with higher Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, but was pushed lower by profit-taking sales," said a trader at a brokerage house.
Swap-related demand seen over the past two days was absent today, said a trader at a city bank.
On Tuesday and Wednesday, some banks which had received fixed interest rates in the interest rate swap (IRS) market bought Euroyen futures for hedging purposes.
"Swap-related demand eased today, and Euroyen futures dipped on profit-taking," the city bank trader said.
The two-year IRS rate was quoted at 0.96/1.00 percent, up from 0.92/0.96 percent on Wednesday. The three-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.32/1.36 percent, up from the previous day's 1.27/1.31 percent.
The volume of the June contract was 81,506 contracts.

"There aren't enough incentives for the market to push Euroyen futures significantly in either direction. The June might just hover around the current level until the release of the Bank of Japan's tankan report," said the city bank trader.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will release its key quarterly survey of corporate sentiment, known as the "tankan", on November 27.
In the interbank call market, the key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.48 percent, down from 0.49 percent on Wednesday.
On Wednesday, the overnight rate edged up due to fund demand related to tax payments, traders said.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected a net 500 billion yen into the money market this morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
The key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were offered at 0.51 percent, down from 0.52 percent on Wednesday.
About 40 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was issued at 0.49 percent, unchanged from the previous day.
